name: Long Method
description: A function has grown so large that nobody can hold its whole flow in their head at once.
cues: body runs well past one screen
distinct phases separated by blank lines
deep nesting of loops and conditionals

name: Large Struct
description: A single type accumulates so many fields and methods that it carries several unrelated jobs.
cues: dozens of loosely related fields
methods touching disjoint field subsets
vague type names like Manager or Context

name: Long Parameter List
description: A function demands so many arguments that call sites become unreadable and easy to get wrong.
cues: four or more parameters
adjacent same-typed arguments easy to swap
boolean flags that switch behavior

name: Primitive Obsession
description: Plain strings and numbers stand in for domain concepts that deserve their own types.
cues: stringly-typed ids compared to literals
unit-less numbers passed around
same raw value re-validated at every use

name: Data Clumps
description: The same group of values travels together through many signatures instead of being one value.
cues: identical parameter trios recur across functions
fields always read or written together
copy-pasted argument groups at call sites

name: Switch Statements
description: Type or tag checks are repeated across the codebase where dispatch should be decided once.
cues: switch or if-else chains on a type tag
same case list duplicated in several places
new variant requires touching every chain

name: Temporary Field
description: A field is only meaningful during certain operations and sits empty the rest of the time.
cues: fields set just before one method call
nil checks guarding usually-unset fields
state that belongs in locals or parameters

name: Refused Bequest
description: A subtype takes on inherited or embedded behavior it does not want and leaves much of it unused or stubbed.
cues: embedded type used for one or two methods
panicking or no-op interface implementations
overrides that discard parent behavior

name: Divergent Change
description: One type keeps changing for several unrelated reasons, revealing that it mixes responsibilities.
cues: unrelated features all edit the same file
method groups that never interact
one struct parses, stores, and renders

name: Shotgun Surgery
description: A single conceptual change forces small edits scattered across many files.
cues: renaming one concept touches a dozen files
same rule redefined in several packages
every feature ships as a ripple of tiny edits

name: Parallel Inheritance Hierarchies
description: Adding a type in one hierarchy always forces adding a mirror type in another.
cues: matching name prefixes across two type families
type pairs created and deleted together
factories updated in lockstep

name: Duplicate Code
description: The same logic lives in more than one place, so every fix must be applied repeatedly.
cues: near-identical blocks differing in one name
sibling branches with the same statements
parallel functions drifting apart over time

name: Dead Code
description: Code that can never run or is never referenced stays in the tree and misleads readers.
cues: unreferenced functions, fields, or variables
branches behind always-false conditions
commented-out blocks kept for someday

name: Speculative Generality
description: Abstraction built for imagined future needs complicates the code without any present payoff.
cues: interface with one implementation and one caller
unused hooks, parameters, or options
generics instantiated with a single type

name: Feature Envy
description: A method spends most of its time working with another type's data rather than its own.
cues: long runs of accessor calls on one foreign value
receiver barely used inside the method
logic about a type living in another package

name: Inappropriate Intimacy
description: Two types reach into each other's internals so deeply that neither can change independently.
cues: direct pokes at another type's internals
bidirectional references between two types
tests of one type break when the other moves

name: Message Chains
description: A caller navigates a long chain of objects to reach the thing it actually needs.
cues: expressions shaped like a.B().C().D()
callers knowing a nested graph's full shape
deep structural change breaks distant callers

name: Middle Man
description: A type does almost nothing except forward calls to another type.
cues: most methods are one-line delegations
wrapper adds no validation or translation
callers could reach the delegate directly
